MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JANUARY 24, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:05 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Deputy City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Victor Yoo, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Miles Royston, Eagle Scout and Boy Scout Troop 191 led the audience in the Pledge of
Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE RESIDENTIAL REFUSE
  SERVICE

  Arielle Bernard, Waste Management, drew the name of Paul David as the
  recipient of one year’s free disposal service.

  Ms. Bernard reported that AB 341 (Mandatory Commercial Recycling) and AB 1826
  (Recycling Organic Waste) have gone into effect for businesses and multi-family
  dwellings. Customers may contact Waste Management for a waste assessment to
  determine what is needed to comply with these new mandates.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – DECEMBER AND JANUARY

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57892 THROUGH 57929 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $315,518.05 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-D.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JANUARY 24, 2017
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

B.  DECEMBER 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  DECEMBER MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FY 2016-17

  APPROVED THE BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2016-17.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

9.  NEW BUSINESS (Taken out of order)

A.  COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT AND RELATED DOCUMENTS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2016

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the draft
  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for fiscal year ended June 30,
  2016 and MGO's Independent Auditor's Report.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead reported that the Tennis Fund, which is now closed and included in
  the General Fund, is shown as a separate fund in this document because it was
  still in existence at June 30, 2016. He also noted that the Equestrian Fund
  will be closed as of the next quarter and will also be included in the General
  Fund.

  Jim Godsey, MGO, provided an extensive presentation of the Comprehensive
  Annual Financial Report (CAFR).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted her concern with the limited term expected
  for the exceptional building permit fees and the future of sales tax revenue as
  both relate to the City’s long-term fiscal health.

  Mr. Godsey noted that most cities have similar challenges.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN referred to the history of permit fees in the CAFR.
  He noted that Administrative Services Director Whitehead has prepared a model
  proforma that shows expected permit income and where this will lead in the
  future. Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that they have
  worked with a financial adviser and concluded that there will be increased
  building permit revenues over the next few years, although staff can only
  estimate which fiscal year the development fees will come through the City.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested reviewing this item at the Policy
  Development Session.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired as to how many of Mr. Godsey’s clients
  have utility user tax fees. Mr. Godsey replied that the majority of his clients do
  have those fees in place and that more and more cities are charging fees for
  services since they do not require a vote.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 24, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN then inquired about the PERS discount rate. Mr.
  Godsey stated that PERS provides mostly estimates so the actual number is not
  known at this time. He reminded COUNCIL that, although the required level of
  funding appears large, PERS operates over a thirty year horizon, and that the
  City need only pay the amount demanded each year to satisfy its obligations.

  Brief discussion ensued regarding deferred maintenance of streets, storm
  drains and other infrastructure.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Mr. Godsey noted that the annual
  required PERS contribution will more than likely increase.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that staff is making PERS Unfunded
  Liability Payments in a lump sum early in the fiscal year to avoid the high
  discount rate being levied throughout the year.

  City Manager Prichard also noted that PERS decisions impacting all cities are
  out of their control and that Rolling Hills Estates has done everything it can do
  over the past several years to mitigate its costs, including bonding for the Side-
  Fund, paying off the pre-2013 UAL in lump sum, creating multiple benefits tiers
  and exchanging the Employer Paid Member Contribution benefit for salary.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE DRAFT COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL
  FINANCIAL REPORT (CAFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2016
  AND MGO’S INDEPENDENT AUDITOR’S REPORT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

10.  OLD BUSINESS (Taken out of order)

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR CITY HALL AND CITY COUNCIL
  CHAMBERS REDESIGN AND UPGRADE PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the specifications and bid
  documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the City Hall and City
  Council Chambers Redesign and Upgrade Project.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that he would like to see a phased in
  approach. He then inquired if solar tubes were considered for some of the
  lighting as he did not see it identified in the specifications and suggested
  including this as a separate item. Administrative Services Director Whitehead
  noted that this will be looked at when the City Hall roof is being replaced.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN referred to the American Disabilities Act (ADA)
  requirements in regards to the City Hall restrooms and the need to make them
  compliant.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE SPECIFICATIONS AND BID DOCUMENTS AND
  AUTHORIZED THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE CITY HALL AND
  CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS REDESIGN AND UPGRADE PROJECT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that more information will be needed in
  regards to the cost for storm drain improvements before this project moves
  forward.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that an amendment to the cleaning and
  inspection contract for storm drains will be brought back to the COUNCIL at
  the meeting of February 14.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 24, 2017
 7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  CAL WATER PRESENTATION FOR PIPELINE PROJECT

  Robert Kuta, Vice President, Engineering, California Water, provided an update
  on the PV Pipeline Project noting that this effort will address the Peninsula’s
  aging water infrastructure and increase reliability.

  Carmelo Sorce, Director, Engineering, California Water, provided an extensive
  presentation regarding the alignment that was presented to the COUNCIL in
  March 2016. He noted that they have created a better design which would
  bypass Buckskin and Dapplegray Lanes and will extend further along Palos
  Verdes Drive North onto the Dapplegray School property. He further noted that
  this will minimize homeowner impacts as well as the Chandler Preserve.
  Additionally, he stated their plan to begin construction in January 2018 with
  an expected completion date at the end of 2019.

  After extensive discussion it was generally considered a superior alignment.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2388 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF 2017-18
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing; 2)
  Receive any public testimony; 3) Close the public hearing; 4) Waive further
  reading and approve Resolution No. 2388 authorizing execution of a contract
  with the Los Angeles County Community Development Commission for
  participation in the program for funding the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk
  Improvement Program as identified in the Program and Conditions Assessment
  Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount of approximately $21,845.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN regarding a budget adjustment for
  this item, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the amount presented
  was likely carried over from last year.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that  these  types  of  project
  improvements are expensive, but much needed.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2388 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES APPROVING THE
  CITY’S PARTICIPATION IN THE FEDERAL HOUSING & URBAN
  DEVELOPMENT (HUD) PROGRAM THROUGH THE LOS ANGELES
  “URBAN COUNTY” PROGRAM, PROGRAM YEAR 2017-2018 AND
  AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY  COMMUNITY  DEVELOPMENT  COMMISSION  FOR
  PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM FOR FUNDING OF THE “ADA
  ACCESS RAMP & SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM.”

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 24, 2017
 9.  NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JANUARY 17, 2017

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF JANUARY 17, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  DECEMBER 19, 2016 – HORSE TRAINER PERMIT FEES

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the proposed three categories of
  Horse Trainer permit fees with the exception that: 1) Category 3 Horse Trainer
  permit fees would increase by $100 for calendar year 2017 and an
  undetermined fee for 2018; 2) Rolling Hills Estates Resident's Horse Trainer
  permit fees would remain at $150 for calendar year 2017; and 3) Category 2
  Horse Trainers shall be defined as operating their primary business outside of
  Los Angeles County as listed in the categories of the staff report.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO ADOPT THE PROPOSED THREE CATEGORIES OF HORSE TRAINER
  PERMIT FEES WITH THE EXCEPTION THAT: 1) CATEGORY 3 HORSE
  TRAINER PERMIT FEES WOULD INCREASE BY $100 FOR CALENDAR
  YEAR 2017 AND AN UNDETERMINED FEE FOR 2018; 2) ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES RESIDENT'S HORSE TRAINER PERMIT FEES WOULD
  REMAIN AT $150 FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2017; AND 3) CATEGORY 2
  HORSE TRAINERS SHALL BE DEFINED AS OPERATING THEIR
  PRIMARY BUSINESS OUTSIDE OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY AS LISTED
  IN THE CATEGORIES OF THE STAFF REPORT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 712 SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CALIFORNIA AMENDING SECTION 1.12.010 OF CHAPTER 1.12
  (ELECTIONS), AMENDING SECTION 2.04.020 OF CHAPTER 2.04 (CITY
  COUNCIL), AND ADOPTING PROCEDURES TO CONSOLIDATE ITS MUNICIPAL
  ELECTIONS WITH STATEWIDE JUNE ELECTIONS PURSUANT TO SENATE
  BILL 415 BEGINNING IN 2018, AND TO EXTEND THE TERMS OF EXISTING
  COUNCIL MEMBERS AS A RESULT OF THE MANDATED CHANGE IN THE
  CITY'S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION DATE.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 712.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 712 by title only.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 24, 2017
 12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  60TH ANNIVERSARY SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 17, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE 60TH ANNIVERSARY SUBCOMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF JANUARY 17, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested securing a 1957 Two-Door Coupe or
  Convertible for the Holiday Parade in honor of the year the City was
  incorporated.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that a Mayor’s Golf Tournament at
  the new Rolling Hills Country Club was discussed at a prior COUNCIL meeting.

B.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the SBCCOG Homeless Services
  Committee met and thanked the volunteers who participated in the homeless
  count.

C.  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ reported that she attended the California Contract
  Cities Association Legislative Tour Conference with staff and invited
  Assemblyman Muratsuchi to take a tour of the City. She noted that this will be
  scheduled soon.

D.  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ reported that she met with Supervisor Hahn and
  her Field Deputy Mark Waronek in an effort to forge a relationship with the new
  representatives. She noted that they discussed transportation as well as other
  regional issues.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquiring about the Supervisor’s
  discretionary funds, City Manager Prichard responded that while the budget is
  being developed, the City will get advanced notice on if those funds will be
  available.

E.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL announced that the SBCCOG General Assembly
  is scheduled for February 24 at the Carson Community Center and all
  COUNCIL MEMBERS, Commissioners, Committee Members and residents are
  invited to attend.

F.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL announced that the Air Resources Board has
  released their plan under SB 350 for reduction of greenhouse gas emissions
  and how cities will deal with this issue.

G.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL announced that an air quality plan hearing has
  been scheduled by the Air Quality Management District (AQMD) on May 3,

B.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked the staff for ordering an extra amount of sand
  bags (that were available to Peninsula residents at Howlett Park and the Fire

  City Manager Prichard also thanked the staff for their involvement in
